title: Board contract files with no approval notice citing them
question: Since notices began to carry the Board file number, does every Board-approved contract of $100,000 or more have one?
finding: Nearly all do. Of 719 contract, grant, lease and loan files of $100,000 or more that passed from 2020 to 2026, 687 (95.5%) are cited by file number on a notice. 32 are not: 20 name only a public body and 12 name a private party, the largest being File 220145 (Tumbleweed Energy Storage LLC, $65,000,000). 3 of the 12 concern an organization that already has a case file on this site.
how: Board files are the passed contract, grant-agreement, lease and loan files in this project’s table of money files whose title amount is $100,000 or more; grants the City accepts, settlements and files where the City is paid are left out. A file has a notice when its six-digit number appears in the file-number box of any notice in either filing system. Before 2020 the box was mostly left empty, so earlier years cannot be tested this way. A file naming only public bodies is counted and not listed; code changes and agreements that bring revenue to the City through an administrator are left out.
limits: A notice may exist under a mistyped or missing file number, or under the name of a parent or partnership; an amount read from a title can be a ceiling the contract never reached; a lease in which the City is the landlord and an agreement with a utility or a grant administrator may fall outside the rule. Each row is a question for the Clerk of the Board: was a notice filed, and under what number?
